incident.title: Checkout requests failing with HTTP 500
symptoms: Checkout error rate above 20% since about 10:05 UTC

facts.statement: checkout-svc v2.3.1 ('Discount engine refactor') was deployed at 10:02:00Z, about 3 minutes before errors began.
checkout-svc ERROR logs from 10:04:51Z onward show a NullPointerException in PriceCalculator.applyDiscount and name v2.3.1. POST /checkout returns 500 with the same exception.
checkout-svc error_rate_pct went from 0.4 at 10:00Z to 23.5 at 10:06Z.
A config change at 09:58Z set search-svc cache.ttl_seconds from 300 to 60.
checkout-svc depends on payments-svc and pricing-db, and web-frontend calls checkout-svc. search-svc does not appear among checkout-svc's neighbours.

assumptions.statement: payments-svc and pricing-db were healthy during the window.
assumptions.basis: Their log queries for the window came back empty, but no errors in the logs does not prove they were healthy, and I did not check their metrics.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Query metrics for payments-svc and pricing-db (error rate, latency) for 09:45–10:30Z.

assumptions.statement: The high CPU on checkout-svc is a side effect of the exceptions and failing requests, not a separate capacity problem.
assumptions.basis: Only one CPU sample was returned, at 10:06Z, so there is no pre-deploy baseline to compare against.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Pull node_cpu_pct for 09:30–10:30Z and see whether CPU was already high before 10:02Z.

assumptions.statement: Rolling back to the version before v2.3.1 would bring the error rate back down.
assumptions.basis: Timing, plus the stack trace pointing at the refactored discount code.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Roll back checkout-svc and watch error_rate_pct.

hypotheses.summary: The v2.3.1 discount engine refactor added a null-handling bug in PriceCalculator.applyDiscount, causing NPEs and HTTP 500 on POST /checkout.
pricing-db returned missing or null discount data, which surfaces as an NPE in applyDiscount.
CPU saturation on the checkout-svc nodes is causing request failures.
The search-svc cache TTL reduction at 09:58Z caused extra load that indirectly affects checkout.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back checkout-svc from v2.3.1 to the last known-good release. Then confirm that the POST /checkout 5xx rate falls back to its pre-10:05 UTC baseline.
recommended_actions.rationale: H1 is the top hypothesis at 0.85 and nothing contradicts it. The v2.3.1 deploy (deploy:inc01:0001) lines up with the error spike (metric:inc01:err:0001, metric:inc01:err:0002) and with the NPE stack traces in PriceCalculator.applyDiscount (log:inc01:0003, log:inc01:0004, log:inc01:0006). A rollback is the fastest way to bring the error rate down, and it also tests H1: if the errors stop afterward, H1 is confirmed.

recommended_actions.action: Review the v2.3.1 diff of PriceCalculator.applyDiscount for the null-handling regression. Add a regression test with null or absent discount input before redeploying the discount engine refactor.
recommended_actions.rationale: This confirms the root cause in code and stops the same defect from coming back when the refactor ships again.

recommended_actions.action: Check the pricing-db responses for the failing requests in log:inc01:0004 to see whether discount fields are actually missing or null at the source. Compare the rate of null discount data before and after 10:05 UTC.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 has low confidence (0.07), but it shares log:inc01:0004 with H1. If pricing-db really is returning nulls, then a rollback that hides the NPE could also hide a data problem. This check tells us whether the fix needs a data correction too, or only defensive code.

recommended_actions.action: Check checkout-svc CPU after the rollback. If it normalizes along with the errors, treat the CPU spike as a symptom and not the cause.
recommended_actions.rationale: H3 rests on a single CPU metric (metric:inc01:cpu:0001), and the NPE logs contradict it. Checking CPU after the rollback lets us rule it out without spending effort on capacity changes.
